genxml.title: O2 MACE two-wire (I2C) bus interface
genxml.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 149 to 151 and 181)
genxml.doc: MACE two-wire bus interface: the configuration and reset register, its alias, the control and status register and the data register. Offsets are from the block base (constant BLOCK_BASE).

struct.name: CONFIG
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 149 to 151 and 181)
struct.doc: Bus configuration and reset, bits 5:0 (established, printed pages 150 and 151, tables 76 and 79). Bits 0 to 3 are read/write and reset to zero. Bits 4 and 5 are read-only input levels with no fixed reset value, so the register has no single reset value (table 79 marks them X).

struct.name: CONFIG_ALIAS
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 149 to 151 and 181)
struct.doc: Labelled reserved in the register table, with the note that it aliases the configuration register above. Bits 5:0 only (established, printed page 150, table 76). This section records no access to it.

struct.name: CONTROL
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 149 to 151 and 181)
struct.doc: Control and status, bits 7:0. Bits 0, 1 and 2 are read/write; bits 4, 5 and 7 are read-only status; bits 3 and 6 are reserved read-only, kept for compatibility with the VINO interface (established, printed page 150, table 77). Every bit resets to zero.

struct.name: DATA
struct.from: published MACE 2.0 I/O ASIC specification (printed pages 149 to 151 and 181)
struct.doc: Bus data, bits 7:0, reset to zero (established, printed page 150, table 78). The register text says a write starts a write cycle when control bit 1 is one, and a read starts a new read cycle. Control bit 1 is one for read in table 77 (printed page 150), so the two tables disagree about the write case. The disagreement is not resolved here (see docs/mace-video.md).
